title: Distinguish advisory identity from npm's fixAvailable presentation
context: Upstream narrowed the advisory range (>=1.25.0 → 1.25.0 - 1.29.0) and npm majors disagree on fixAvailable shape (object vs boolean for identical locks). Audit gate must re-review without false positives.
decision: Split comparison semantics: advisory identity (source, range, severity, nodes, effects, via) stays byte-exact; fixAvailable uses semantic comparison (both objects → exact match, otherwise → truthiness only).
consequences: Audit gate tolerates npm version presentation variance while catching real advisory changes
Advisory identity remains exact and verifiable across npm versions
No false positives when npm majors disagree on fixAvailable shape
alternatives_rejected: Byte-exact JSON comparison on all fields (breaks on npm major transitions)
Normalize fixAvailable to boolean (loses fix-detail semantics needed elsewhere)
Skip fixAvailable comparison entirely (misses real security regression)
